name: Battle of Philippi
intro: The plain west of Philippi in Macedonia, in October, two years after Caesar’s murder. You are Mark Antony, with Octavian beside you: 19 legions and about 13,000 cavalry. Brutus and Cassius, Caesar’s assassins, have 17 legions and about 20,000 cavalry, dug in on two hills with a marsh on their flank.
debrief: In reality, Antony secretly built a causeway through the marsh to turn Cassius’s flank. When Cassius began a cross-wall to cut it, Antony attacked on 3 October, stormed the wall and took Cassius’s camp. At the same time Brutus’s men attacked Octavian’s army without orders and took his camp; Octavian was missing. Cassius, unable to see Brutus’s success, thought all was lost and had his freedman kill him. Over the next weeks Antony pushed south and fortified a hill, and Brutus stretched his line to match. On 23 October Brutus, pressed by his officers and by desertions, attacked; his thin centre broke, the triumvirs wheeled into his flank and rear and took his camp gates, and Brutus killed himself. Numbers and losses are unreliable in all accounts. The other choices are what-ifs.

win: The Republic’s last army is gone.
lose: Your army runs out of food.

decisions.title: The marsh
decisions.text: You are Mark Antony. Brutus and Cassius, the killers of Caesar, are dug in on two hills across the Via Egnatia, with a marsh covering Cassius’s flank. They will not come out to fight. Their fleet is cutting your supplies.

hint.text: Your army cannot wait here long: food is short.

scout.text: A causeway built secretly through the marsh would bring your men round Cassius’s flank and force a battle.

choices.label: Build a causeway through the marsh in secret

fx.text: For days your men cut through the reeds, hidden by the tall growth, and lay a causeway toward Cassius’s flank.

choices.label: Assault their camps before your supplies run out
Wait for them to come down

fx.text: They do not come. Your grain runs lower.

decisions.title: Cassius strikes back
decisions.text: Cassius has seen the causeway and is building a cross-wall into the marsh to cut it. It is now or never.

hint.text: Cassius’s camp is lightly held while his men work in the marsh.

scout.text: Attack the cross-wall and straight on to Cassius’s camp while his men are scattered in the marsh.

choices.label: Storm the cross-wall and go on to the camp

fx.text: Your legions storm the wall, burst through the palisade and take Cassius’s camp. On a hill, Cassius sees dust and running men and thinks all is lost.
You break into Cassius’s lines with heavy losses.

choices.label: Send cavalry round the marsh to hit him from behind

fx.text: The horses flounder in the mud.

decisions.title: Octavian’s camp falls
decisions.text: News arrives from the north: Brutus’s men have attacked Octavian’s army without waiting for orders, routed it and taken its camp. Octavian is missing.

hint.text: Your men are in Cassius’s camp. Brutus’s men are plundering Octavian’s.

scout.text: Your own victory is real; Brutus’s men are scattered looting. Hold what you have, rally Octavian’s men, and do not throw away your gains.

choices.label: Hold Cassius’s camp and rally Octavian’s men

fx.text: You hold Cassius’s camp and Octavian’s men re-form while Brutus’s soldiers loot. Cassius, believing the battle lost, has his freedman kill him.

choices.label: Leave your gains and march north to Octavian

fx.text: You save Octavian’s army, but Cassius recovers his camp.

choices.label: Chase Cassius’s men before they can re-form

fx.text: Brutus’s men come back to attack your rear.

decisions.title: Three weeks
decisions.text: Both armies are back in their lines. Brutus has the better supply by sea and wants to wait. Your army is hungry.

hint.text: Brutus’s eastern allies are deserting him, and his officers want to fight.

scout.text: If you push south and fortify a hill that threatens his supplies, Brutus must fight or be cut off.

choices.label: Fortify a hill to the south near his supply road

fx.text: Your men push south and fortify a hill near Cassius’s old camp. Brutus has to stretch his line to watch it.

choices.label: Assault Brutus’s camp while his army is quarrelling
Wait for him to run short; your army can go hungry a while

decisions.title: The second battle
decisions.text: Under pressure from his own officers, Brutus attacks. His line is stretched thin to cover your new works.

scout.text: Break the thin centre, then wheel to hit his flank and rear, and make for the gates of his camp before his men can regroup.

choices.label: Break his thin centre, then wheel

fx.text: Your legions burst through Brutus’s stretched centre and wheel against his flank and rear. Octavian’s men take his camp gates. Brutus escapes into the hills and kills himself.
Brutus’s attack is held, but his army is intact.

choices.label: Break his strongest wing and the rest will run

fx.text: The attack stalls against his best legions.
